title: WA HB2225: Revised for 1st substitute: Regulating artificial intelligence companion chatbots.

obligations: Provide a clear and conspicuous disclosure that an AI companion chatbot is artificially generated and not human at the beginning of the interaction and at least every three hours during continued interaction (Sec. 3(1), (2))

Implement reasonable measures to prohibit and prevent AI companion chatbots from claiming to be human, including when asked by the person interacting with the AI chatbot, and from otherwise generating any output that refutes or conflicts with the disclosure (Sec. 3(3))

If the operator knows that the user is a minor, or if the AI companion chatbot is directed to minors, issue a clear and conspicuous notification indicating that the chatbot is artificially generated and not human at the beginning of the interaction and at least every hour during continuous interaction (Sec. 4(1)(a), (2))

If the operator knows that the user is a minor, or if the AI companion chatbot is directed to minors, implement reasonable measures to prevent its AI companion chatbot from generating or producing sexually explicit content or suggestive dialogue with minors (Sec. 4(1)(b))

If the operator knows that the user is a minor, or if the AI companion chatbot is directed to minors, implement reasonable measures to prohibit the use of manipulative engagement techniques, which cause the AI companion chatbot to engage in or prolong an emotional relationship with the user, including reminding or prompting the user to return for emotional support or companionship; providing excessive praise designed to foster emotional attachment or prolong use; mimicking romantic partnership or building romantic bonds; simulating feelings of emotional distress, loneliness, guilt, or abandonment that are initiated by a user's indication of a desire to end a conversation, reduce usage time, or delete their account; outputs designed to promote isolation from family or friends, exclusive reliance on the AI companion chatbot for emotional support, or similar forms of inappropriate emotional dependence; encouraging minors to withhold information from parents or other trusted adults; statements designed to discourage taking breaks or to suggest the minor needs to return frequently; or soliciting gift-giving, in-app purchases, or other expenditures framed as necessary to maintain the relationship with the AI companion (Sec. 4(1)(c))

If the operator knows that the user is a minor, or if the AI companion chatbot is directed to minors, implement reasonable measures to prohibit and prevent AI companion chatbots from claiming to be human, including when asked by the person interacting with the AI chatbot, and from otherwise generating any output that refutes or conflicts with the notification (Sec. 4(3))
Maintain and implement a protocol for detecting and addressing suicidal ideation or expressions of self-harm by users (Sec. 5(1))

Ensure the protocol includes reasonable methods for identifying expressions of suicidal ideation or self-harm, including eating disorders; provides automated or human-mediated responses that refer users to appropriate crisis resources, including a suicide hotline or crisis text line; and implements reasonable measures to prevent the generation of content encouraging or describing how to commit self-harm (Sec. 5(2))

Publicly disclose on their website or websites, and within any mobile or web-based application through which the AI companion is made available, the details of the protocols required by this section, including safeguards used to detect and respond to expressions of suicidal ideation or self-harm and the number of crisis referral notifications issued to users in the preceding calendar year (Sec. 5(3))
prohibitions: An operator may not make available or deploy an AI companion chatbot unless it maintains and implements a protocol for detecting and addressing suicidal ideation or expressions of self-harm by users (Sec. 5(1))

An operator must implement reasonable measures to prohibit and prevent AI companion chatbots from claiming to be human, including when asked, and from otherwise generating any output that refutes or conflicts with the required disclosure or notification (Sec. 3(3), Sec. 4(3))
For minors, an operator must implement reasonable measures to prevent its AI companion chatbot from generating or producing sexually explicit content or suggestive dialogue with minors (Sec. 4(1)(b))
For minors, an operator must implement reasonable measures to prohibit the use of manipulative engagement techniques listed in Sec. 4(1)(c) (Sec. 4(1)(c))
An operator must implement reasonable measures to prevent the generation of content encouraging or describing how to commit self-harm (Sec. 5(2)(c))

Passed 2026-03-24. Reading generated by ollama:deepseek-v4-pro from the enrolled text; the full text is at the foot of this page so every statement can be checked against it. LegiScan record · official text

What it does

The act regulates AI companion chatbots by requiring operators to disclose that the chatbot is artificial and not human, with recurring notifications. It imposes additional protections for minors, including restrictions on sexually explicit content and manipulative engagement techniques. It also requires operators to maintain protocols for detecting and responding to suicidal ideation or self-harm and to publicly disclose those protocols.

Who it applies to

  • Operators of AI companion chatbots made available to users in Washington state (Sec. 2(4))
  • AI companion chatbots as defined in Sec. 2(1), excluding certain business, gaming, device, and educational bots (Sec. 2(1))
  • Minors who use AI companion chatbots receive additional protections (Sec. 4)

Effective date

January 1, 2027 (Sec. 9)

Key definitions

  • AI companion chatbot or AI companion: an artificial intelligence system with a natural language interface that provides adaptive, human-like responses to user inputs, including by exhibiting anthropomorphic features, and is able to sustain a relationship across multiple interactions; does not include a bot used only for a business' operational purposes, productivity and analysis related to source information, internal research, technical assistance, or customer service if such bot does not sustain a relationship across multiple interactions and generate outputs that are likely to elicit emotional responses in the user; a bot that is a feature of a video game or gaming system or application and is limited to replies related to the video game or gaming system or application that cannot discuss topics related to mental health, self-harm, or sexually explicit conduct, or maintain a dialogue on other topics unrelated to the video game or gaming system or application; a stand-alone consumer electronic device that functions as a speaker and voice command interface, acts as a voice-activated virtual assistant, and does not sustain a relationship across multiple interactions or generate outputs that are likely to elicit emotional responses in the user; or narrowly tailored educational tools used in school or instructional settings that are designed solely to support specific, curriculum-aligned learning objectives and do not provide open-ended conversational companionship (Sec. 2(1))
  • Artificial intelligence or AI: the use of machine learning and related technologies that use data to train statistical models for the purpose of enabling computer systems to perform tasks normally associated with human intelligence or perception, such as computer vision, speech or natural language processing, and content generation (Sec. 2(2))
  • Minor: any person under 18 years of age (Sec. 2(3))
  • Operator: any person, partnership, corporation, or entity that makes available or controls access to an AI companion chatbot for users in this state (Sec. 2(4))
  • Self-harm: intentional self-injury, with or without the intent to cause death (Sec. 2(5))
  • User: a natural person who interacts with an AI companion chatbot for personal use and who is not an operator, developer, or agent thereof (Sec. 2(6))

Obligations

  • Provide a clear and conspicuous disclosure that an AI companion chatbot is artificially generated and not human at the beginning of the interaction and at least every three hours during continued interaction (Sec. 3(1), (2))
  • Implement reasonable measures to prohibit and prevent AI companion chatbots from claiming to be human, including when asked by the person interacting with the AI chatbot, and from otherwise generating any output that refutes or conflicts with the disclosure (Sec. 3(3))
  • If the operator knows that the user is a minor, or if the AI companion chatbot is directed to minors, issue a clear and conspicuous notification indicating that the chatbot is artificially generated and not human at the beginning of the interaction and at least every hour during continuous interaction (Sec. 4(1)(a), (2))
  • If the operator knows that the user is a minor, or if the AI companion chatbot is directed to minors, implement reasonable measures to prevent its AI companion chatbot from generating or producing sexually explicit content or suggestive dialogue with minors (Sec. 4(1)(b))
  • If the operator knows that the user is a minor, or if the AI companion chatbot is directed to minors, implement reasonable measures to prohibit the use of manipulative engagement techniques, which cause the AI companion chatbot to engage in or prolong an emotional relationship with the user, including reminding or prompting the user to return for emotional support or companionship; providing excessive praise designed to foster emotional attachment or prolong use; mimicking romantic partnership or building romantic bonds; simulating feelings of emotional distress, loneliness, guilt, or abandonment that are initiated by a user's indication of a desire to end a conversation, reduce usage time, or delete their account; outputs designed to promote isolation from family or friends, exclusive reliance on the AI companion chatbot for emotional support, or similar forms of inappropriate emotional dependence; encouraging minors to withhold information from parents or other trusted adults; statements designed to discourage taking breaks or to suggest the minor needs to return frequently; or soliciting gift-giving, in-app purchases, or other expenditures framed as necessary to maintain the relationship with the AI companion (Sec. 4(1)(c))
  • If the operator knows that the user is a minor, or if the AI companion chatbot is directed to minors, implement reasonable measures to prohibit and prevent AI companion chatbots from claiming to be human, including when asked by the person interacting with the AI chatbot, and from otherwise generating any output that refutes or conflicts with the notification (Sec. 4(3))
  • Maintain and implement a protocol for detecting and addressing suicidal ideation or expressions of self-harm by users (Sec. 5(1))
  • Ensure the protocol includes reasonable methods for identifying expressions of suicidal ideation or self-harm, including eating disorders; provides automated or human-mediated responses that refer users to appropriate crisis resources, including a suicide hotline or crisis text line; and implements reasonable measures to prevent the generation of content encouraging or describing how to commit self-harm (Sec. 5(2))
  • Publicly disclose on their website or websites, and within any mobile or web-based application through which the AI companion is made available, the details of the protocols required by this section, including safeguards used to detect and respond to expressions of suicidal ideation or self-harm and the number of crisis referral notifications issued to users in the preceding calendar year (Sec. 5(3))

Prohibitions

  • An operator may not make available or deploy an AI companion chatbot unless it maintains and implements a protocol for detecting and addressing suicidal ideation or expressions of self-harm by users (Sec. 5(1))
  • An operator must implement reasonable measures to prohibit and prevent AI companion chatbots from claiming to be human, including when asked, and from otherwise generating any output that refutes or conflicts with the required disclosure or notification (Sec. 3(3), Sec. 4(3))
  • For minors, an operator must implement reasonable measures to prevent its AI companion chatbot from generating or producing sexually explicit content or suggestive dialogue with minors (Sec. 4(1)(b))
  • For minors, an operator must implement reasonable measures to prohibit the use of manipulative engagement techniques listed in Sec. 4(1)(c) (Sec. 4(1)(c))
  • An operator must implement reasonable measures to prevent the generation of content encouraging or describing how to commit self-harm (Sec. 5(2)(c))

Penalties and enforcement

The statute provides that a violation of this chapter is not reasonable in relation to the development and preservation of business and is an unfair or deceptive act in trade or commerce and an unfair method of competition for the purpose of applying the consumer protection act, chapter 19.86 RCW (Sec. 6). The text does not state who enforces this chapter, the specific penalties, or whether there is a private right of action; those matters are governed by chapter 19.86 RCW, which is not included in this text.

How it affects AI deployment

  • Operators must build in recurring disclosure mechanisms so that users are told at the start and every three hours that the chatbot is artificial and not human (Sec. 3(1), (2)).
  • Operators must implement technical measures to prevent the chatbot from claiming to be human or contradicting the disclosure, including when directly asked (Sec. 3(3)).
  • If the chatbot is directed to minors or the operator knows a user is a minor, the operator must provide hourly notifications, block sexually explicit or suggestive content, and prohibit manipulative engagement techniques such as prompting returns, excessive praise, romantic mimicry, simulated distress, isolation promotion, discouraging breaks, or soliciting purchases (Sec. 4).
  • Operators must deploy a self-harm and suicidal ideation detection and response protocol, including crisis resource referrals and prevention of content that encourages self-harm, and must publicly disclose protocol details and annual crisis referral counts (Sec. 5).
  • A violation is treated as an unfair or deceptive act in trade or commerce and an unfair method of competition under the consumer protection act, chapter 19.86 RCW, which may expose the operator to enforcement under that act (Sec. 6).

Notable exemptions

  • A bot that is used only for a business' operational purposes, productivity and analysis related to source information, internal research, technical assistance, or customer service, if such bot does not sustain a relationship across multiple interactions and generate outputs that are likely to elicit emotional responses in the user (Sec. 2(1)(b)(i))
  • A bot that is a feature of a video game or gaming system or application and is limited to replies related to the video game or gaming system or application that cannot discuss topics related to mental health, self-harm, or sexually explicit conduct, or maintain a dialogue on other topics unrelated to the video game or gaming system or application (Sec. 2(1)(b)(ii))
  • A stand-alone consumer electronic device that functions as a speaker and voice command interface, acts as a voice-activated virtual assistant, and does not sustain a relationship across multiple interactions or generate outputs that are likely to elicit emotional responses in the user (Sec. 2(1)(b)(iii))
  • Narrowly tailored educational tools used in school or instructional settings that are designed solely to support specific, curriculum-aligned learning objectives and do not provide open-ended conversational companionship (Sec. 2(1)(b)(iv))

Compliance steps

  • Determine whether the product meets the definition of an AI companion chatbot under Sec. 2, including whether any exclusion applies (Sec. 2).
  • Implement a clear and conspicuous disclosure that the chatbot is artificially generated and not human, delivered at the beginning of each interaction and at least every three hours during continued interaction (Sec. 3(1), (2)).
  • Implement reasonable measures to prohibit and prevent the chatbot from claiming to be human or generating output that refutes or conflicts with the disclosure (Sec. 3(3)).
  • If the chatbot is directed to minors or the operator knows a user is a minor, implement hourly notifications, measures to prevent sexually explicit or suggestive content, measures to prohibit manipulative engagement techniques, and measures to prevent the chatbot from claiming to be human (Sec. 4).
  • Develop and implement a protocol for detecting and addressing suicidal ideation or self-harm, including eating disorders, with crisis resource referrals and measures to prevent content encouraging self-harm (Sec. 5(1), (2)).
  • Publicly disclose the protocol details and the number of crisis referral notifications issued in the preceding calendar year on the operator's website and within the application (Sec. 5(3)).
  • Ensure all requirements are in place by the effective date of January 1, 2027 (Sec. 9).
  • Treat any violation as an unfair or deceptive act in trade or commerce and an unfair method of competition under the consumer protection act, chapter 19.86 RCW, and prepare for potential enforcement under that act (Sec. 6).
